species.name: Trout
mustRead: speckled spotted flanks
adipose fin
squared-off shallow-forked tail

species.name: Char
mustRead: pale spots on a dark ground (not dark on pale)
white leading edges on lower fins
slender streamlined body

species.name: Lamprey
mustRead: round jawless sucker mouth ringed with rasping teeth
row of seven gill pores behind the eye
finless eel-like body with no paired fins

species.name: Pike
mustRead: long flattened duck-bill snout full of teeth
dorsal fin set far back near the tail
elongate torpedo body with pale bean markings

species.name: Catfish
mustRead: long drooping barbel whiskers around the mouth
broad flattened scaleless head
stiff spine at the front of the dorsal and pectoral fins

species.name: Gar
mustRead: long narrow toothed beak snout
armour of hard diamond scales
dorsal and anal fins set far back near the tail

species.name: Bowfin
mustRead: very long undulating dorsal fin running most of the back
rounded fan tail
bony plate under the chin and a black eyespot near the tail

species.name: Bass
mustRead: spiny front dorsal fin joined to a soft rear one
large hinged bucket mouth
deep laterally compressed body

species.name: Eel
mustRead: continuous fin fringe running along back, tail and belly
no pelvic fins
snake-like body with a blunt-jawed head

species.name: Carp
mustRead: deep heavy-shouldered body
two pairs of barbels at the mouth corners
long single dorsal fin running most of the back

species.name: Tilapia
mustRead: deep laterally flattened disc of a body
long spiny dorsal fin along the whole back
blunt steep forehead

species.name: Piranha
mustRead: very deep chunky body
undershot jutting lower jaw with triangular teeth
steep blunt forehead

species.name: Killifish
mustRead: flattened topped head with an upturned mouth
dorsal fin set far back near the tail
rounded paddle tail fin

species.name: Beluga
mustRead: bulging rounded melon forehead
no dorsal fin, only a low ridge along the back
uniform white body with a visible neck crease

species.name: Narwhal
mustRead: single long spiralled tusk projecting forward from the head
no dorsal fin
mottled grey body with a blunt rounded head
species.note: The tusk grows from the left side of the upper jaw, not from the centre of the snout like a horn.

species.name: Orca
mustRead: tall triangular dorsal fin
crisp black-and-white saddle and eye patches
large rounded paddle pectoral fins

species.name: Right Whale
mustRead: enormous strongly arched jawline taking up a third of the body
crusty white callosity patches on the head
no dorsal fin at all on a smooth broad back

species.name: Arctic Cod
mustRead: slim elongated body with a deeply forked tail
small barbel under the chin
projecting upper jaw and large eye

species.name: Herring
mustRead: streamlined silver body with a keeled belly
single small dorsal fin at mid-back
deeply forked tail and large eye with an upturned jaw

species.name: Blue Whale
mustRead: tiny nub dorsal fin set far back near the tail
broad flat U-shaped rostrum with a single ridge
pleated throat grooves
species.note: Commonly drawn with a large dorsal fin; the real fin is a thumb-sized nub three-quarters back.

species.name: Humpback Whale
mustRead: enormously long white wing-like pectoral flippers
knobbly tubercles on the head and jaw
scalloped trailing edge on the tail flukes

species.name: Cold-Water Fish
mustRead: stout torpedo body
soft-rayed dorsal fin and forked tail
blunt rounded snout with a chin barbel
species.note: Generic name - interpreted as a cod/char-type coldwater bony fish.

species.name: Blind Fish
mustRead: smooth blank eyeless head
pale pinkish unpigmented body
ordinary tetra-like fin layout

species.name: Small Fish
mustRead: simple streamlined silvery body
single dorsal fin mid-back
forked tail
species.note: Generic name - interpreted as a representative minnow-type baitfish.
